A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original configuration appendix matches v3 Appendix B; the added and replaced material can be identified reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original 30-seed simulation results, semi-synthetic Cora experiments, negative controls, and architectural, noise, sample-size, and topology analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a quantitative hub-threshold sweep and supplementary statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The residual-based R-Learner objective, four nuisance/final-stage configurations, and GNN components are retained. 'Sanity Check' becomes 'Hybrid R-Learner' without a procedural change. The expanded explanations and initialization disclosure do not establish an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: Both versions retain BA, ER, SBM, semi-synthetic Cora, and the same causal mechanisms and negative control. The hub-threshold sweep analyzes retained network data. Appendix A's new star graph is an analytical example, not an additional empirical benchmark.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in corresponding experiments remain unchanged: the four R-Learner configurations and external GNN T-Learner. Hybrid R-Learner matches the earlier Sanity Check, and the external baseline's treatment-conditioned single-GNN procedure is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 Section 6.3 introduces evaluation across hub thresholds from the top 2.5% to 25% of nodes by degree, supplementing the retained top-10% hubs/bottom-50% periphery comparison. The six configuration blocks retain identical sample sizes, model settings, training budgets, and learning rates.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 replaces the qualitative t-SNE representation analysis with a quantitative test of whether the hub-performance inversion persists across degree thresholds. Appendix C.1 adds a parameter-count comparison addressing capacity explanations. This substantially revises the supplementary evidence, while retaining the original negative control and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 30-seed means, standard deviations, and p-values. v3 Appendix C newly identifies paired t-tests, describes seed-level resimulation, and adds Holm-Bonferroni correction across four topologies. The new sweep uses the existing 30-seed/standard-deviation reporting practice; no increase in the established run count is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain their numerical results, including Graph R-Learner MSEs of 0.5165 on BA and 0.3352 on Cora. v3 adds hub-threshold results and adjusted p-values, and removes the t-SNE findings. Table 7 introduces an unresolved discrepancy: its Cora raw p-value is 1.44e-2, whereas retained Table 4 reports 1.41e-2.

T1.justification: Although both abstracts promise a constructive example, only v3 supplies it: Appendix A adds a five-node star construction and an argument claiming that flexible graph-blind models must fail. This is substantive new formal reasoning. However, its constraints f(1)=f(2)=sin(10) and f(10)=sin(1.25) are compatible, so the claimed impossibility is not established.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: final-stage representation dominates nuisance quality, nuisance performance depends on topology, and the work supplies a reproducible benchmark. The revised conclusion reinforces this existing hierarchy with additional supporting analyses without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: v3 removes the interpretation of t-SNE clusters as learned causal representations, expands the over-squashing explanation around the threshold sweep, and reframes sample efficiency as stability under data scarcity. New future-work discussion identifies unmatched parameter budgets, incomplete degree-regime characterization, and untested domain generalization; the impact statement adds applicability cautions.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository address, component and total parameter counts, and Xavier-normal initialization with fixed seed 0 for the DGP GNNs. These supplement the unchanged YAML configurations. They are additional reproducibility disclosures, not evidence that the underlying architecture or initialization procedure changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Barabási and Albert, Guo et al., Ma et al., Rubin, and Veličković et al., and removes Robinson's semiparametric-regression reference. These support background and implementation explanations; the positioning relative to Khatami et al. and the claim of systematic dissection remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. Local revisions expand the DML tutorial and identification explanation, rename Sanity Check, replace Section 6.3, and add future-work, impact, and appendix sections. These are focused revisions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes from a t-SNE scatterplot to a hub-threshold error-bar plot. Figure 3's unchanged panels are enlarged and arranged vertically across a full page, and Tables 6–7 are added. Figure 1's model label, several captions, figure/table placement, and publication headers also change.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the threshold sweep, multiple-comparison correction, code address, and implementation disclosures improve empirical support and reproducibility. However, the new Appendix A introduces an invalid impossibility argument: a graph-blind function can satisfy all its stated constraints. The sweep also does not isolate over-squashing despite stronger mechanistic assertions. These useful additions and new validity problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
